main.note: mainline extractors + verifier + native schema/verifier contracts

sarol.note: Sarol-variant adjudicator + the enum contract and rubric guidance it was split into (OQ8 resolved 2026-09-01)

combined_hash_recipe: sha256 over the concatenation, in ascending path order, of '<path>\0<sha256>\n' for every entry. Each entry sha256 is over the raw bytes of `git show <source_refs[entry.source].commit>:<entry.path>`.

output_vocabulary.contract: FIXED. The optimizer may edit every part of the rubric that makes it good -- definitions, boundaries, worked examples, tie-breaks, the worst-wins ordering -- but NOT the set of emittable labels, because the benchmark defines it and the scorer consumes it. The optimizer prompt must state this enum explicitly. A prediction outside it is an invalid output: scored as a miss and counted in error_class_counts, never a crash and never silently re-bucketed.
output_vocabulary.why_no_collapse_needed: This variant emits Sarol's gold vocabulary directly, so every gold label is reachable and 3-way macro-F1 is directly comparable to the published baselines. The mainline-plus-collapse alternative left 17 of IRRELEVANT's 34 instances structurally unreachable -- see the plan's Part A2.

runtime_pins.why: The extractor prompt loads the paperclip command reference at run time via `paperclip skill`; the in-repo SKILL.md is a 10-line stub. That reference is outside the frozen fileset, so without this pin two runs of one program version could diverge with no manifest diff.
